title: SYMBIOGENESIS x model-merge alpha-sweep — synergy vs least-bad-blend
method: two specialist linear maps A,B fit by closed-form least-squares (Cramer 3x3) each to a DISTINCT sub-task; merge W(a)=a*A+(1-a)*B; grade on the COMBINED task loss=(1/2N)[||X t - yA||^2 + ||X t - yB||^2]; sweep a in {0.0..1.0 step 0.1}; measure loss(W(a)) for the full grid

config.design_matrix: fixed deterministic 12x3 integer X (full column rank, det(X'X)=17082)
config.fit_recovery: exact (N>d, targets in column space; residual ~0) — validity gate F314.2 PASS

asymmetric_probe.note: decisive discriminator — B niche scaled 3x (thetaB2_true=3*thetaB). If the optimum left 0.5 and beat the naive midpoint, that would be real interior structure (synergy). It did NOT.

falsifiers.F314.2_FIT_VALID: PASS (specialist A residual on its own task ~0; exact recovery)
falsifiers.F314.5_DETERMINISM: PASS (loss(W(0.5)) re-run identical; cross-process fresh run byte-identical: sym 11.3906, asym 45.599)

synergy_test.requirement: NOT monotone AND interior optimum below both endpoints AND (asymmetric) optimum OFF the naive midpoint 0.5 AND loss(a*) strictly below loss(0.5)

finding: There IS a non-trivial interior dip (symmetric: 11.39 at a=0.5, ~50% below either specialist's 22.78; asymmetric: 45.60 at a=0.5 below 91.20). BUT the optimum is the least-squares AVERAGE of the two fits and stays GLUED to the naive midpoint a=0.5 even under a 3x-asymmetric niche — it never moves off 0.5 and never beats the naive midpoint-average expectation. The dip is the trivial geometry of a convex bowl (averaging two equidistant minimizers), NOT synergy. Merge = least-bad blend, not symbiosis. Matches governance a_completeness_over_cheap: 'model-merge of two failures = least-bad midpoint' is a known LIMITATION, not a win.
verdict_derivation: DERIVED from the measured loss(a) grids above — NOT self-declared. The numbers (argmin at 0.5, optimum == naive midpoint, no off-midpoint shift under asymmetry) FORCE the closed-negative; a different curve (optimum off-0.5 beating the midpoint) would have read SUPPORTED. The computation could have falsified the verdict either way.
honest_scope: linear least-squares toy (d=3, N=12), convex quadratic union-loss. 'synergy' operationalized as a non-trivial off-midpoint interior optimum on the union-loss. NOT a claim about real neural-network model merging (task arithmetic / TIES / SLERP), where non-linearity could in principle produce true synergy. This probe rules out synergy ONLY for the linear-merge-of-linear-specialists regime.

tier.numbers: GREEN NUMERICAL (deterministic closed-form least-sq + arithmetic, byte-reproducible cross-process)
tier.empirical_interpretation: WHITE SPECULATION-FENCED (the symbiosis reading is metaphor, not an atlas identity)
